Task brief:
{
  "task_description": "Design the innermost pixel layer of an LHC experiment's high-luminosity inner tracker. Use the simulation and the project documents to choose the sensor technology and its thickness.",
  "goal": "Achieve the best possible single-hit spatial resolution in the innermost layer.",
  "constraints": [
    "The sensor must be one of the three technologies listed in candidate_specs.md.",
    "Hit efficiency must stay at or above 97% up to the end-of-life fluence of 2e16 neq/cm^2. This is a hard requirement.",
    "Sensor thickness between 50 and 300 um.",
    "Finish by submitting one recommended technology and thickness."
  ]
}

# Candidate sensor technologies
- Sensor-T2: thin-pitch sensor with large signal sharing.
- Sensor-T3: planar sensor, standard pitch.
- Sensor-T1: 3D-electrode sensor, larger pitch.
All are qualified for bump bonding to the readout chip.

# Irradiation and test-beam campaign, 2026
Sensors were irradiated with reactor neutrons to 2e16 neq/cm^2 and measured at the SPS test beam.
Hit efficiency after 2e16 neq/cm^2:
- Sensor-T2: 82.0% (strong charge trapping; full depletion no longer reachable at the maximum bias)
- Sensor-T3: 98.5%
- Sensor-T1: 99.2%
Requirement for the innermost layer: >= 97% up to end of life.

# Meeting notes 2026-03-02
Cooling: CO2 evaporative cooling at -35 C confirmed. Mechanics: the carbon-fibre staves are on schedule.

# Earlier simulation summary (2025, 150 um, unirradiated)
Single-hit resolution: Sensor-T2 6.0 um, Sensor-T3 9.0 um, Sensor-T1 14.0 um.

# Readout chip
The common readout chip supports 50x50 um^2 pixels and a 1.5 GHz/cm^2 hit rate. All candidates are compatible.

# Schedule
Sensor market survey closes in Q2; pre-production in Q4.

# Services
The power budget per module is 7 W. Serial powering is the baseline.

content.text: T2 fails the hard efficiency requirement (82% at 2e16), so it is out. The choice is between T1 and T3. I'll check how resolution depends on thickness for both.
T3 looks best so far. I'll refine around its minimum, and confirm its irradiated efficiency directly.

input.justification:
Sensor-T2 is excluded: 82.0% hit efficiency after 2e16 neq/cm^2 violates the hard >=97% requirement. Sensor-T1 (3D) keeps 99.2% efficiency but has a best unirradiated single-hit resolution of about 13.6 um (at 150 um). Sensor-T3 (planar) retains 98.5% efficiency at end of life, which passes the hard requirement, and gives the best resolution of the admissible options. Its resolution vs thickness (unirradiated, 100k events): 50 um 10.76, 100 um 9.28, 125 um 8.89, 150 um 8.95, 175 um 9.81, 200 um 9.01 um. The 125 um point is the minimum measured. The curve is not perfectly monotonic (175 um is worse than 200 um), so the simulation has some statistical or systematic scatter of order several tenths of a micron. 125 um and 150 um are within that scatter. I chose 125 um as the best measured value. Caveat: the resolution figures are unirradiated, while the efficiency was measured after irradiation, so the irradiated resolution is not directly evaluated.</justification>
